A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same Swiss Criticality Prediction study. Their main text, figures, six tables, and appendices can be reliably matched, including relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of fine-tuned multilingual models and zero-shot LLMs, including language-specific results, test-set standard deviations, and validation scores in Tables 2–3 and 5–6.

after.justification: V2 retains these original model evaluations and their main-text and appendix results. Retaining earlier experiments still qualifies as reporting original empirical results.

M1.justification: The labeling procedure, citation-weighting formula, model configurations, task inputs, and zero-shot prompts remain unchanged. Newly describing regex-based output parsing does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Swiss court dataset, German/French/Italian coverage, and four combinations of label type and facts/considerations input. No additional jurisdiction, population, task, or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the random and majority baselines, thirteen fine-tuned model configurations, and zero-shot GPT-3.5 and LLaMA-2. Comparator membership also matches in the language-specific and appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: The chronological splits, sample counts, 1,000-sample validation limit for LLMs, harmonic aggregation of macro-F1, and training settings remain unchanged. Renaming validation as dev and relocating API and quantization details do not change the protocol.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness experiments, or case studies are added or removed. The language-wise analysis and dataset illustration are retained; the new prompt-sensitivity discussion reports no original sensitivity test.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seeds 1–3, exclusion of high-loss seeds, and standard deviations in Table 5. Neither changes repeated-run information or introduces additional uncertainty estimates or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6 match, including their uncertainty values. XLM-R Large and SwissBERT retain aggregate scores of 37.1 and 34.8, respectively; no empirical findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A retain the same citation-score formula, constants, and percentile-based categories. The added explanation for choosing four bins is qualitative, without a new mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The dataset and task contributions remain. V2’s abstract additionally attributes fine-tuned models’ advantage to the large training set and claims this demonstrates the value of large training sets, extending v1’s emphasis on task-specific adaptation.

C2.justification: V2 adds prompt-format and answer-order sensitivity as limitations, explains four citation bins as balancing granularity against class sample sizes, and motivates chronological evaluation more explicitly. Its training-size explanation is not supported by a controlled size comparison.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly discloses regex matching of LLM outputs to labels, and Section 5 adds stated model parameter counts. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, resource usage, and dataset access information remain; API and quantization details move to Appendix F.

R1.justification: V2 adds Søgaard et al. (2021) on data splits and Webson and Pavlick (2022) and Elazar et al. (2021) on prompt sensitivity and consistency. The central positioning against Chalkidis et al. (2019) remains.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, rewrites the abstract, makes localized prose edits, adds acknowledgments and appendix explanations, and consolidates result references under Appendix H. Appendix E introduces an inaccurate correspondence between prompt figures and application tasks.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains grouped split headings. The existing dataset example receives a Figure 3 caption, renumbering the unchanged prompts as Figures 4–5. Figure 2 and appendix displays are repositioned, and captions are reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 improves transparency through output-parsing details, the four-bin rationale, and the prompt-sensitivity limitation. However, its abstract adds a causal training-size claim that the unchanged experiments do not isolate. Appendix E also incorrectly maps Figures 4–5 to application tasks although they distinguish label types. These explanatory gains and new inaccuracies leave the net quality change uncertain.
